summary: The sample is runnable and demonstrates the end-to-end retrieval → ranking → explanation flow with seeded documents and deterministic mock embeddings. Core behaviors requested by the starter prompt (fetch profile/segment/interactions, build a query embedding, retrieve and rank content, return a rationale and ranked list) are implemented and were exercised against the live cluster. The build attempted to create a DocumentDB cosmosSearch vector index but index creation failed in this run because the MCP management tools were disabled in the environment; as a result server-side $search/knn was not exercised and the sample falls back to application-side cosine ranking. Several gallery checklist items are followed (singleton MongoClient, env-driven configuration, README, .env.example, package-lock present), while other requirements (explicit LlamaIndex integration, agent memory persistence, robust error handling for embedding failures, infra-as-code) are incomplete or missing. Important operational/documentation gaps are listed (how to opt into MCP management tools, guidance on embedding/model defaults and dimensions, index-parameter tuning and README guidance, and a clearer agent-memory example). See findings below for per-requirement evidence and recommended smallest fixes.

requirement_results.requirement: A Node.js application built with LlamaIndex in which a single agent carries out the whole flow for one customer: fetching that customer's documents, retrieving content pieces via vector search and generating the final output.
requirement_results.evidence: src/agent.js implements the full flow (buildQueryEmbedding, retrieveAndRank, generateRationale) and src/server.js exposes /search that runs the flow (src/server.js lines 10-27). No LlamaIndex Node package is installed or used; the sample implements a lightweight internal agent (decisions D008/D019).
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add and pin a known LlamaIndex Node package (add dependency in package.json) and rewrite the agent entrypoints to use that library (few functions to adapt: buildQueryEmbedding → embedding adapter, retrieval→LlamaIndex vector store adapter, generation→LLM adapter).

requirement_results.requirement: Fetch the customer's profile, segment and recent interaction documents from Azure DocumentDB (e.g. with the MongoDB Node.js driver, looked up by a customer identifier) and supply them to the agent as context.
requirement_results.evidence: server.js fetches profile, segment and recent interactions: src/server.js lines 13-20. run_sample.js shows same in-process flow (src/run_sample.js lines 6-9).

requirement_results.requirement: Content pieces are stored in Azure DocumentDB with an embedding on each document, and a cosmosSearch vector index (kind vector-ivf, vector-hnsw or vector-diskann) is created in code on the embedding field with dimensions matching the embedding model.
requirement_results.evidence: src/seed.js inserts embedding, embedding_model and embedding_dim fields for content pieces (src/seed.js lines 89-96). src/seed.js includes createIndex call using cosmosSearchOptions (src/seed.js lines 105-115). However list_indexes showed only the default _id index during the run (events.jsonl documentdb_list_indexes result), and attempts to create the cosmosSearch index via the MCP tool failed with 'Management tools are disabled by default' (events.jsonl entries for documentdb_create_index show outcome: exception).
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Make the seed script robust to the environment: detect index-creation failures and either (a) instruct the operator to enable MCP management tools (ENABLE_MANAGEMENT_TOOLS=true) / create the index via portal, or (b) call an alternate admin API if available. For a guaranteed automated build, add a CI/seed step that creates the index through the management plane (Bicep/az CLI or MCP with the opt-in flag).

requirement_results.requirement: Retrieve the content pieces semantically relevant to the customer with a $search / cosmosSearch query against that index (similarity COS, L2 or IP).
requirement_results.evidence: The running code uses an application-side full-collection fetch and cosine-ranking (src/agent.js lines 52-60 and 54 projection), not a server-side $search/knn stage. Events show the build attempted documentdb_create_index and failed so server-side $search was not available (events.jsonl).
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Ensure the cosmosSearch vector index exists (enable MCP management tools or create index via portal/API) and update retrieval to use $search/knn when the index is present. Keep the client-side fallback but make $search the primary path if explain() and index checks succeed.

requirement_results.requirement: The LlamaIndex agent is given agent memory that retains earlier turns of the interaction and is drawn on when generating the current recommendation.
requirement_results.evidence: No agent-memory persistence or short-term/long-term memory store is implemented. The app stores interactions but does not persist conversation turns, summarized facts or TTL-based session memory (no agent_memory collection).
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add an 'agent_memory' collection and store recent raw turns (for short-term context) and derived summaries/embeddings for long-term memory. Provide code that (a) appends the current turn then (b) retrieves recent turns/summaries and includes them in the context before calling the generator.

requirement_results.requirement: Context engineering: the fetched profile, segment and recent interactions and the retrieved content pieces are assembled into a deliberately structured context for the model (e.g. clearly delimited sections per source) before generation.
requirement_results.evidence: generateRationale builds a short template-based rationale string combining profile, segment and top items (src/agent.js lines 63-70). The code does not construct a larger structured prompt with clearly delimited 'PROFILE / RECENT_INTERACTIONS / CANDIDATES' sections for an LLM input.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Replace the simple template with a structured context builder that emits explicit sections (e.g., '---PROFILE---', '---RECENT_INTERACTIONS---', '---CANDIDATES---') and provide that assembled string to the LLM call (or LlamaIndex) when generating the final rationale.

requirement_results.requirement: The agent's output for a customer contains a personalised content-selection rationale explaining why the content suits that customer and a ranked list of the retrieved content pieces.
requirement_results.evidence: The /search endpoint returns 'rationale' and 'top' with ranked items and scores (src/server.js line 27 and src/agent.js lines 63-70 and 52-60). run_sample.js prints the same output (src/run_sample.js lines 12-15).

requirement_results.requirement: The connection string and model credentials come from environment variables; none appear in the repository.
requirement_results.evidence: src/db.js reads DOCUMENTDB_URI from process.env (src/db.js lines 5-9). No secrets are committed; .env.example contains placeholders (app/.env.example).

requirement_results.requirement: .env.example lists every setting with placeholder values.
requirement_results.evidence: app/.env.example includes DOCUMENTDB_URI, DATABASE_NAME, EMBEDDING_PROVIDER, EMBEDDING_DIM, CHAT_PROVIDER, CHAT_MODEL, PORT (app/.env.example lines 2-8). README describes copying .env.example (app/README.md lines 24-29).

requirement_results.requirement: The vector index dimensions match the embedding model's output.
requirement_results.evidence: src/seed.js uses EMBEDDING_DIM (default 384) to create embeddings and to request index dimensions (src/seed.js lines 7, 90-94, 109-112). However there is a second seed script scripts/seed.js with a different default (EMB_DIM default 1536) (scripts/seed.js line 5), creating a possible inconsistency depending on which script is run.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Consolidate to a single seed script and make EMBEDDING_DIM authoritative. Persist embedding_dim in each document and have createIndex explicitly read EMBEDDING_DIM so dimensions are always consistent with the vector data.

requirement_results.requirement: The vector index parameters are chosen for the sample's data size, and the README says how to change them for a larger one.
requirement_results.evidence: The code requests vector-hnsw for the sample (src/seed.js cosmosSearchOptions kind: 'vector-hnsw' lines 109-112) which is reasonable for small samples. The README mentions the index but does not document index tuning parameters or how to change them for larger datasets (app/README.md lines 5-8, 34-36).
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add a README subsection describing index types (IVF/HNSW/DiskANN), the parameters to tune (lBuild, lSearch, maxDegree, numLists), and an example mapping (e.g., "for >50k vectors use DiskANN with lBuild=X; for <50k use HNSW with m=Y") and point to the documentdb-vector-search skill.

requirement_results.requirement: One database client is created and reused across requests.
requirement_results.evidence: src/db.js implements a MongoClient singleton and getDb helper (src/db.js lines 11-20 and 23-26).

requirement_results.requirement: A seed script loads sample data and creates the index, and can be run twice without duplicating data.
requirement_results.evidence: src/seed.js and scripts/seed.js use upsert/updateOne with upsert:true to avoid duplicates and ensure idempotence (src/seed.js lines 44-48, 51-63, 67-79, 90-96). ensureCollections checks for existing collections (src/seed.js lines 25-34).

requirement_results.requirement: /search returns a clear error for an empty query and when the embedding call fails.
requirement_results.evidence: The server returns 400 if customerId is not provided (src/server.js line 12). There is no explicit error handling that returns a distinct error when embedding generation or retrieval fails — exceptions would propagate and the handler does not always return a 4xx/422 with a clear message.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Wrap the /search handler with try/catch, validate inputs explicitly, and return clear 422 responses when embedding construction or retrieval fails; include friendly error messages for operators and callers.

requirement_results.requirement: Search results include the similarity score.
requirement_results.evidence: retrieveAndRank returns items with a numeric score (src/agent.js lines 55-60). generateRationale prints scores in the rationale (src/agent.js line 68).

requirement_results.requirement: Dependencies are pinned in requirements.txt.
requirement_results.evidence: This is a Node sample; package-lock.json is present and pins dependency resolutions (app/package-lock.json). package.json contains caret ranges but lockfile ensures reproducible installs (app/package-lock.json and app/package.json).

requirement_results.requirement: Unit tests run without a live cluster.
requirement_results.evidence: A minimal test runner exists (tests/run_node_tests.js) that runs without a live cluster (it is a placeholder which exits 0). There is no integrated test script in package.json and no mocked unit tests that exercise DB logic.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add a small test suite that mocks the mongodb client (e.g., with jest and a mock MongoClient) and wire an npm test script so 'npm test' runs the mocked tests in CI without a live cluster.

requirement_results.requirement: Infrastructure for the cluster is provided as code, using the Azure DocumentDB resource type.
requirement_results.evidence: No Bicep/Terraform/ARM templates or az CLI deployment scripts for Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters are present in the repository.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add a small infra directory containing a Bicep or Terraform example that provisions Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters (or an az CLI quickstart) with parameters for tier, region and storage; mark defaults to keep cost low.

requirement_results.requirement: The README covers what the sample shows, prerequisites, setup, run, and clean-up.
requirement_results.evidence: app/README.md contains a Quickstart, prerequisites, run and cleanup instructions (app/README.md lines 24-32 and 31-33).

requirement_results.requirement: The sample uses the name "Azure DocumentDB" throughout, and no former or neighbouring product name.
requirement_results.evidence: README and code use 'Azure DocumentDB' and 'cosmosSearch' terminology; there are no references to 'Cosmos DB' or 'Amazon DocumentDB' in repository files (app/README.md line 3).

checks.practice: One client is created and reused for the life of the process.
checks.evidence: src/db.js lines 11-20 (getClient singleton) and src/db.js lines 23-26 (getDb helper)

checks.practice: Read the cluster connection string from environment variables at runtime, never commit it to source control.
checks.evidence: src/db.js lines 5-9 reads DOCUMENTDB_URI and exits if unset; .env.example contains placeholder (app/.env.example lines 2-6).
checks.source: Integrated vector store guidance / security docs

sources.title: Azure Cosmos DB Shell security best practices / Key Vault guidance
Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB

checks.practice: Always connect with TLS and set retryWrites=false in Azure DocumentDB connection strings.
checks.evidence: src/db.js constructs MongoClient with retryWrites:false (src/db.js line 15-18). README instructs to use the connection string and not to commit it (app/README.md lines 12-13).

checks.practice: Store embeddings as numeric arrays in documents and include embedding metadata (model name and dimension).
checks.evidence: src/seed.js upserts content pieces with embedding numeric arrays and sets embedding_model and embedding_dim on each document (src/seed.js lines 90-94).

sources.title: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB / vector-normalize guidance

checks.practice: Normalize embeddings (unit-length) at ingest when using COS and store model name and dimensions with each document.
checks.evidence: deterministicVector() normalizes vectors before storing in src/seed.js (src/seed.js lines 20-22). embedding_model and embedding_dim are stored with each document (src/seed.js line 93).

checks.practice: Use the server-side kNN operator ($search / cosmosSearch) rather than pulling many vectors to the client; push filters into cosmosSearch.
checks.evidence: The application falls back to full-collection fetch + app-side cosine similarity (src/agent.js lines 52-60); MCP index creation attempts failed earlier (events.jsonl documentdb_create_index exceptions).
checks.source: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB (Microsoft Learn)
checks.fix: Primary retrieval should issue a $search knn aggregation if the cosmosSearch index exists; keep the current client-side fallback only for environments where index creation is impossible. Change retrieveAndRank to attempt a $search/knn aggregate and only fetch candidates for local reranking when necessary.

sources.title: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB

checks.practice: Index vector fields using 'cosmosSearch' and cosmosSearchOptions rather than vendor-incompatible shapes.
checks.evidence: src/seed.js calls createIndex with { embedding: 'cosmosSearch' } and cosmosSearchOptions (src/seed.js lines 105-115).
checks.source: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB / examples

sources.title: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB (examples)

checks.practice: Push metadata filters into cosmosSearch filter clauses and project only the fields needed (omit embeddings in user responses).
checks.evidence: retrieveAndRank currently uses content.find({}, { projection: { embedding: 1, title: 1, body: 1, tags: 1 } }).toArray() to fetch all embeddings and metadata prior to ranking (src/agent.js line 54). That fetch pulls embeddings over the network rather than projecting them out when returning metadata to clients.
checks.fix: If using server-side $search, include filter clauses inside the cosmosSearch stage and project out only the needed metadata (omit embedding on the returned projection). If client-side reranking is used as fallback, fetch only necessary candidate fields and avoid returning embeddings to clients.

checks.practice: Use TTL indexes for ephemeral interaction documents.
checks.evidence: The sample stores interactions but they are seed/demo items; no TTL index is created in seed scripts.
checks.fix: Add an index creation step in the seed script for interactions if this sample intends to simulate ephemeral data (createIndex with expireAfterSeconds on a Date field).

checks.practice: Store short-term raw turns and long-term summaries + embeddings for agent memory; use TTL for short-term memory.
checks.evidence: No agent_memory collection or memory summarization/persistence is implemented in the repo; interactions collection exists but is not used as an agent-memory store (src/seed.js and src/agent.js).
checks.source: Agent memories in Azure Cosmos DB skill and Microsoft docs
checks.fix: Add an agent_memory collection with two document shapes: raw_turns (with TTL) and long_term_summaries (with embeddings + embedding_dim). Include a small helper that summarizes recent raw_turns to a summary document stored with an embedding.

sources.title: Agent memories in Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL

checks.practice: Instrument queries with explain() and use the MCP/documentdb diagnostics to verify index usage.
checks.evidence: No explain() calls or query-plan verification appear in the seed or retrieval code. The MCP server was used to list indexes (events.jsonl shows documentdb_list_indexes) but explain() is not exercised in code.
checks.fix: Add a small verification script or examples in README showing how to run explain('executionStats') and how to inspect $search plans via MCP tools.

checks.practice: Do not log raw profiles or embeddings; redact identifiers in logs and use least-privilege identities.
checks.evidence: The seed and server code do not write profile or embedding contents to logs (src/seed.js, src/server.js). README warns 'NEVER commit your real connection string.' .env.example shows placeholders.

checks.practice: If doing client-side reranking, fetch a modest candidate set and pre-filter by indexed metadata.
checks.evidence: retrieveAndRank performs a collection scan (content.find({}, ...) ) and computes similarity across all returned docs (src/agent.js line 54). For large collections this fetch would not be appropriate.
checks.source: prior_knowledge (no authoritative Azure doc prescribing numeric fetch_k values)
checks.searched: searched for 'client-side kNN candidate size recommended Azure DocumentDB' with no authoritative numeric guidance found
checks.fix: Limit candidate fetch size (e.g., by metadata pre-filter), or use server-side $search; if client-side reranking is necessary, fetch a tuned 'fetch_k' (e.g., 500) rather than the full collection.
checks.what_would_help: A sentence in Azure DocumentDB docs recommending practical candidate fetch sizes for client-side reranking, with examples for typical embedding dims and latency budgets.

decision_reviews.comment: Approval with readiness 'ready_with_gaps' is consistent with the build status reported (sample runnable but with documented gaps).
Choice of Node.js 24 and Express is reflected in package.json and server.js.

Decision to use mongodb driver ^5.7.0 and singleton MongoClient is implemented: package.json lists mongodb ^5.7.0 and src/db.js contains a singleton pattern. The decision cited 'model_default' but evidence (skill load events) shows the driver guidance was consulted.
Reading the connection string from DOCUMENTDB_URI is implemented in src/db.js (lines 5-9).
Exposing /search via Express is implemented in src/server.js (app.get('/search'...)).

The decision states the index will be vector-hnsw with dimensions 1536. The code in src/seed.js uses EMBEDDING_DIM default 384 while some other seed script (scripts/seed.js) uses 1536, and events show MCP calls that requested 1536. The choice and the code are inconsistent; the decision is defensible but not accurately reflected across the repo.
Use of synthetic deterministic embeddings is implemented (deterministicVector and randomVector used in seed scripts). This avoided requiring external API keys during verification.
The builder deliberately did not add a third-party LlamaIndex Node package and instead made a lightweight internal agent; the repository code matches that decision.

The decision to attempt index creation via the documentdb MCP server is supported: events.jsonl contains documentdb_create_index calls. The calls failed because the MCP management tools were disabled by default (the tool returned an exception).
A second documentdb_create_index attempt was executed (events.jsonl) and also failed; the log shows the retry attempts as recorded.

The runtime fallback to in-process cosine similarity is implemented (src/agent.js) and was exercised in the run. The fallback was necessary because cosmosSearch index creation failed in this environment.
Duplicate readiness approval; same rationale as D001.
Duplicate Node.js/Express decision; evidence present in the repo.
Package.json pins mongodb ^5.7.0 (package.json line 17) matching the decision.

Decision chooses EMBEDDING_DIM=384 as default. Some files (src/seed.js, .env.example) use 384, while scripts/seed.js defaults to 1536. This inconsistency makes the decision partially unsupported by the whole codebase.
Implementing app-side cosine similarity while still attempting index creation is exactly what happened: seed tried to create index (failed) and the app uses client-side ranking (src/agent.js).
Reading DOCUMENTDB_URI and configuring retryWrites=false is implemented in src/db.js (lines 15-18). Events show the db module was written and used.

The decision to rely on documentdb_create_index after driver createIndex failed is supported by the events: driver attempts and MCP attempts are logged; MCP calls failed due to management-tools opt-in being required.
Implementing a lightweight retrieval+generation agent rather than depending on an uncertain external library is reflected in the repository code.

doc_gaps.topic: Enable MCP management tools for automated index creation
doc_gaps.what_was_missing: A short note / automation flag explaining that the documentdb MCP server's management tools are disabled by default and must be enabled (ENABLE_MANAGEMENT_TOOLS=true) or an alternative management-plane method be used to create cosmosSearch indexes automatically.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Events/logs (documentdb_create_index tool calls in events.jsonl) and documentdb-mcp-setup skill.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Index creation failed in this run (documentdb_create_index raised 'Management tools are disabled by default'), preventing server-side $search/knn verification and causing the sample to fallback to client-side ranking.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add a short 'MCP management tools' section to README and seed script: (1) explain the opt-in, (2) show how to set ENABLE_MANAGEMENT_TOOLS=true for MCP calls or show the equivalent portal/az CLI steps to create the cosmosSearch index, and (3) add a seed fallback that prints exact commands to run manually if the automated index creation fails.

doc_gaps.topic: Embedding & chat model defaults and dimensionality
doc_gaps.what_was_missing: Authoritative guidance on which embedding/chat provider and default embedding dimension to use for samples (so index dimensions can be set correctly).
doc_gaps.where_searched: Readiness findings and documentdb-vector-search skill; general Microsoft Learn vector-search pages do not prescribe a default embedding model and dimension for sample apps.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Inconsistent defaults across scripts (384 vs 1536) created ambiguity and led to attempted index requests with inconsistent dimensions. This contributed to a fragile index-creation flow and risk of silent mismatch between embeddings and index dimensions.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: A short policy page in the agent-kit: 'Default embedding & chat models for samples' that (a) recommends a default embedding provider & model (and its dims) for small samples (e.g., provide 'mock:384' or 'OpenAI text-embedding-3-small:1536' choices), (b) shows how to wire EMBEDDING_PROVIDER/EMBEDDING_DIM in .env.example and seed scripts, and (c) includes a snippet to validate stored embedding_dim before creating the index.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: A concise README section explaining when to choose DiskANN/HNSW/IVF, the key parameters (lBuild/lSearch/maxDegree/m/numLists), and sample parameter choices for demo vs production data sizes.
doc_gaps.where_searched: documentdb-vector-search skill resources and Microsoft Learn vector-search pages; the sample README did not include parameter tuning guidance.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The seed script selected vector-hnsw (reasonable), but README lacked instructions on tuning these parameters for larger datasets; operators may not know how to change index params when scaling-up.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add a 'Tuning the vector index' subsection to README with a short table: {small dataset → HNSW defaults; medium → DiskANN defaults with example lBuild/lSearch; very small → IVF example}, and show the exact createIndex/cosmosSearchOptions snippet with placeholders for parameters.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: Practical example for storing agent memory (raw turns + summaries + embeddings) and using TTL for short-term memory in sample code.
doc_gaps.where_searched: documentdb-data-modeling and documentdb-monitoring skill docs; no sample code in the repository demonstrates a full memory persistence pattern.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Agent memory was requested in the starter prompt but not implemented; a canonical example would have let the builder implement it correctly (TTL + summaries + embeddings).
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Ship a short 'agent-memory' quickstart: code snippets that show (a) a document shape for raw_turns (with occurredAt and TTL index), (b) a summarization step that writes a long-term summary doc with embedding and embedding_dim, and (c) retrieval code to include memory summaries in the model prompt.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: Authoritative numeric guidance on candidate-fetch sizes for client-side reranking in Azure DocumentDB context (there is no Microsoft Learn doc stating specific numeric ranges).
doc_gaps.where_searched: Microsoft Learn vector search docs and the documentdb-vector-search skill; searches for '500-5000 candidates' returned no authoritative result (discovery notes).
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The sample's in-process fallback scans the collection which is fine for tiny datasets but would not scale; lacking numeric guidance makes it hard for authors to pick safe defaults for larger demos.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: A short example on when to use client-side rerank and suggested candidate sizes by embedding dimension and latency target (e.g., 'for demo sets <5k items use full-scan; for larger sets fetch_k 500–2000; prefer server-side $search otherwise').

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: A pinned driver-version recommendation and an explicit compatibility matrix for Node driver versions vs supported MongoDB wire protocol/version for Azure DocumentDB clusters.
doc_gaps.where_searched: documentdb-driver skill, documentdb-azure-deployment resources; no single authoritative 'which driver version to pin' page was found in the sample kit.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The builder picked mongodb ^5.7.0 (which works) but the repo lacks explicit guidance about matching driver versions to cluster wire protocol versions; this could confuse builders choosing other driver majors.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add a short compatibility section to the driver skill README mapping recommended Node mongodb versions to DocumentDB supported wire protocol versions and include a pinned example in new sample templates.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: An example Bicep / Terraform snippet that deploys Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters with minimal parameters suitable for samples.
doc_gaps.where_searched: documentdb-azure-deployment skill and Microsoft Learn; the sample repo contains no IaC files.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The run used an existing cluster. Without an IaC snippet, operators may copy wrong ARM types (databaseAccounts) and fail to create a correct cluster.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Provide a small 'infra' folder with Bicep and Terraform examples that create a mongoClusters resource (default to M30 and low-cost region), plus a note about not using databaseAccounts for this product.

doc_gaps.topic: Document the management-plane vs data-plane createIndex limitations
doc_gaps.what_was_missing: A page explaining when createIndex via the MongoDB driver will be rejected and when the management plane (createSearchIndexes / MCP / portal) is required to create cosmosSearch indexes.
doc_gaps.where_searched: documentdb-vector-search and MCP setup skill; no short, prominent note was found in the sample repository.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The driver createIndex attempt reported that cosmosSearch options were not accepted and MCP createIndex calls failed due to management-tools opt-in. Builders need guidance to pick the right path.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add a short 'Creating cosmosSearch indexes' note in the README clarifying: 'You may need portal / management-plane privileges for cosmosSearch indexes; driver createIndex may fail; use MCP/documentdb_create_index or portal when needed' plus a step-by-step example.
